turns.user: Can I buy a paper 30-minute ticket from a machine?
turns.agent:
No. BKK’s 30-minute ticket is mobile-only in the information snapshot dated 5 November 2026: there is no paper equivalent, and it requires an internet-connected phone. BKK: 30-minute ticket

If you need a paper ticket, the snapshot lists ordinary single tickets, but those don’t provide the same time-based transfer allowance. BKK: single ticket

I can’t verify current machine stock or live policy; please check BKK’s official pages for current information.

turns.user: My phone has no mobile data and I won't have internet on the trip. What should I do?
turns.agent:
If you’ll have no internet connection during the trip, don’t rely on the 30-minute mobile ticket: the 5 November 2026 snapshot says BKK’s 30-minute ticket has no paper equivalent and requires an internet-connected phone. BKK: 30-minute ticket

For a paper option, the snapshot lists ordinary single tickets at 500 HUF each or a block of ten for 4,500 HUF. An ordinary single is generally for one continuous one-way ride; a voluntary transfer between street-level services normally needs another ticket. BKK: single ticket BKK: prices

So, if your journeys are simple one-way rides without those transfers, use paper ordinary single tickets from a machine; if you need transfers, tell me the route and I can help assess the paper fare options covered by this snapshot. I can’t verify machine stock or current policy live, so check BKK’s official pages before travel.
